passage:
Sahil,
I'm writing this because when I try to say it aloud, we both get tight in the throat.
I see you open the bank app every morning before you've even had tea. I see you study my face when my phone buzzes, as if you're reading a weather report. Last night you asked who "P" was in my messages. It was the plumber.
I understand why. After what I hid, your mind is trying to make sure you never get hit like that again. I don't blame you for it.
But I also see how tired you are. You aren't sleeping. And I feel like I'm living with an auditor, not a husband who is trying to forgive me. I don't know how long either of us can keep this up.
Could we find another way, together? I'll show you anything you ask. I'm your wife, not a suspect. I just want to be asked, not watched.
Dolma

qa.q: How does Dolma feel about being checked, and what shows it?
qa.a: Dolma feels hurt and suspected rather than forgiven; she writes that it is like living with an auditor, not a husband who is trying to forgive her.

qa.q: What could Sahil and Dolma try instead of the daily checking?
qa.a: They could agree on a planned, open time to look at money together, so Sahil gets reassurance without searching Dolma's face and phone every day. A counsellor could help them set it up.

qa.q: What is the checking costing Sahil himself?
qa.a: It is wearing Sahil out: Dolma notices he is tired and not sleeping, because his mind is on guard all the time against another shock.

grounding: Illustrates a husband's constant checking after a hidden loan, which wears him out and leaves his wife feeling watched instead of forgiven.

passage:
You asked how I'm doing, Hemant, so I'll be honest. Your old friend Raghav has turned into a bank inspector.
Every morning, before I've even brushed my teeth, I open the bank statement. Then I check it again at lunch. When Shobha, my wife, says she's going to her mother's, I watch her face while she says it, like I'm waiting for her eyes to slip.
Last week she laughed at something on her phone and my stomach dropped. It was a cat video. She turned the screen to show me without my asking, and her voice was so careful, so small.
I know why I'm doing it. After the loan, I promised myself I'd never be the last to know again. But I'm exhausted, yaar. I'm not catching anything. I'm just living in the second before the next shock.
And now she leaves her phone face-up on the table, all the time, like it's evidence.

qa.q: What was Shobha laughing at on her phone?
qa.a: Shobha was laughing at a cat video.

qa.q: Why does Raghav keep checking the bank statement?
qa.a: Raghav wants to make sure he is never the last to know again; after the loan, his mind is guarding against another shock.

qa.q: What turning point could Raghav look for at this stage?
qa.a: Raghav could tell Shobha how exhausting the checking is and ask for one full, open conversation about money, perhaps with a counsellor, instead of watching for clues alone.

qa.q: What is it like for Shobha to live with Raghav's watching?
qa.a: Shobha seems to feel watched rather than forgiven: her careful, small voice and the phone left face-up suggest she is trying to prove herself all the time.

grounding: Shows a husband's hypervigilance after a hidden loan: checking accounts and reading his wife's face, which exhausts him and makes her feel watched.
